title: Build the model for thousands of units, and show it is the same model

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: Makes the reference builder's model, with the same variables in the same order, the same row names, bounds and coefficients, and the same objective coefficients to 1e-9, in time that grows with the fleet: group the candidates by substation, region and kind once, build each sum with mathopt.fast_sum, and take the objective's coefficients from risk_table.
blueprint.idea: Index once and never scan the fleet inside a loop over groups; build sums in one call.

blueprint.signature: def risk_table(units: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> np.ndarray
blueprint.contract: An array with a row per unit and a column per plan year, entry [i, j] equal to risk_removed(units[i], the j-th plan year, request), computed with numpy arrays one kind at a time.
blueprint.idea: A coefficient that is a sum over years is a matrix product over arrays of ages and years.

blueprint.signature: def build_reference(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: The builder of the step before, unchanged: one plain loop per row family, and risk_removed for each coefficient.
blueprint.idea: A faster builder is right only if it makes the same model as a slow one you trust, so keep the slow one and compare.

lesson.title: 14.3.5 From 500 to 5,000 Transformers: Building the Model at Scale

blueprint.contract: The same request for a fleet factor times larger: budget, outages, crew_weeks and each kind's spares times factor (a limit that is None stays None); everything else, the outage cost included, unchanged.
blueprint.idea: A limit is a quantity of the fleet's resources and grows with it; a price or a rate does not.

lesson.title: 14.3.5 From 500 to 5,000 Transformers: Building the Model at Scale

cases: the fast builder makes the reference builder's model, row for row
the risk table matches the coefficient function for every unit and year
a scaled request grows every limit with the fleet and keeps the outage price
